solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Gremlin that diverts English prof's little (12, two words)

indicators.note: to divert something is to turn it from its course, so the following letters are turned into a new order

explanation.surface: A mischievous spirit distracts an English professor's small child.
explanation.walkthrough: ESPRIT FOLLET is French for a hobgoblin or mischievous sprite, used in English too.
explanation.definitionFit: Both name a small mischievous imp blamed for things going wrong, the French term being a household sprite.

clue.text: Foreign cash I added to pay once

parts.note: sold is an archaic word for pay or wages

explanation.surface: Someone tops up a payment that was made in a single instalment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Once' signals an old usage rather than a single time.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldi is the plural of soldo, a former Italian copper coin, so it is foreign money.

clue.text: Justice included in essential life force or understanding of Buddhism

indicators.note: something included in another is put within it

parts.note: prana is the vital breath or life force in Hindu thought
J abbreviates Justice, a judge's title

explanation.surface: Justice forms part of the essential spirit or insight of Buddhist teaching.
explanation.definitionFit: Prajna is the Buddhist term for wisdom or insight into the true nature of reality.

clue.text: Suffering calamities, energy spent, being addicted to faddish ideas

indicators.note: something suffering is in a bad way, so the letters are knocked out of order
something spent is used up and gone, so the letter is removed

parts.note: E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Someone who has suffered disasters and is exhausted takes up passing fads.
explanation.definitionFit: Ismatical describes someone devoted to isms, fashionable theories and doctrines.

clue.text: Good place for pizza or pastry served up

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: a tart is a pastry dish

explanation.surface: Recommending an eatery for pizza or a dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: Trat is a colloquial clipping of trattoria, an Italian restaurant where pizza is served.

clue.text: Cabbage climbing in branch? It's for plucking!

indicators.note: one item is placed inside the next
in a down clue climbing goes upward, so the word reads from bottom to top

explanation.surface: A cabbage growing up through a tree branch, ripe for picking.
explanation.walkthrough: Plucking the forelock (tugging the hair at the brow) is an old gesture of deference; the surface suggests picking fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: The forelock is the lock of hair above the brow, traditionally tugged or plucked as a sign of respect.

clue.text: Floppy disc I'm featured in

indicators.note: something featured in another appears within it

parts.note: an LP is a long-playing record

explanation.surface: Someone says they appear on an old computer floppy disk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Floppy disc' reads as one computing term; Floppy is the definition and disc the record.
explanation.definitionFit: Limp means lacking stiffness, hanging loosely, which is what floppy describes.

clue.text: Gets tips around end of dinner

indicators.note: one item goes around another, enclosing it
the end of a word is its final letter alone

explanation.surface: A waiter collects gratuities at the close of a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tips' suggests gratuities, but it is the verb meaning tilts.
explanation.definitionFit: To get something can mean to understand or grasp it, as in 'I get it', which is to learn it.

clue.text: Sons going forward with a bit of learning, incessant

indicators.note: letters that are going leave the words

parts.note: to forward a letter is to send it

explanation.surface: Boys advancing with some education never stop.
explanation.walkthrough: The S of SEND and the SON of LESSONS go, together spelling Sons, leaving END + LESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Endless means without end or ceasing, the same as unceasing or incessant.

clue.text: Spore cases getting to soak mostly when penetrated by start of rain

definitions.note: a sorus is a cluster of spore cases (sporangia) on a fern frond, so the singular answer names the group

indicators.note: penetrated by means having something driven into it, so the soak word takes a letter inside
mostly means not quite all, so the soak word loses its last letter

parts.note: to souse is to soak or drench

indicators.note: start of asks for the first letter of rain

explanation.surface: Fern spores that get mostly drenched once the rain sets in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' shortens SOUSE to SOUS, and 'when penetrated by' drives in R, the 'start of' rain. 'getting' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: On the underside of a fern frond, each sorus is a cluster of sporangia, the cases that hold spores.

clue.text: Those jabbering to give opinion in press wildly

indicators.note: one item is placed inside the next
acting wildly means out of control, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: to utter is to voice or express a view

explanation.surface: Babbling people air their views in the media chaotically.
explanation.definitionFit: Sputterers are people who speak in hasty, confused bursts, which is jabbering.

clue.text: Projecting angle, one in vaulted passage north of the border

indicators.note: the first item is placed inside the next one

parts.words: vaulted passage north of the border
parts.note: Scots word for an arched passageway; north of the border means Scotland

explanation.surface: An architect describes a protruding corner inside a Scottish arched passage.
explanation.walkthrough: A pend is a covered passage through a building in Scotland; 'north of the border' marks the word as Scots.
explanation.definitionFit: A piend is an architectural term for a salient or hip, a projecting corner where two roof slopes meet.

clue.text: Unenforced law to prevent getting wrongly dealt within

indicators.note: getting something within means receiving it inside

parts.note: to deter is to prevent or discourage

indicators.note: wrongly means incorrectly, so the letters are not in their right order

explanation.surface: A rule meant to stop people getting a bad deal inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A dead letter is a law or rule still formally in force but no longer observed or applied.

clue.text: Bright green stone filled with luminance dad's set before mum

indicators.note: something filled has another item put inside it

parts.note: pa is dad, with the possessive S
L is the symbol for luminance

explanation.surface: A green gem lights up as father places it in front of mother.
explanation.definitionFit: Plasma is a semi-precious variety of chalcedony with a bright green colour, so it names a green gemstone.

clue.text: Some more madeira in fresh rendering

definitions.note: a noun phrase for a past-participle answer; read as something made again

indicators.note: only some of the following words are used, a run of letters inside them

parts.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: A request for another glass of Madeira wine, poured fresh.
explanation.definitionFit: Something remade has been produced anew, a new version or fresh rendering of an earlier work.

clue.text: Couple formerly exhausted tea

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to pair up or breed
second meaning: an obsolete adjective for worn out or overcome
third meaning: the South American herbal infusion, often spelt with an accent

explanation.walkthrough: This is a triple definition: three unrelated senses of the same four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The word works as a verb for pairing animals, an archaic word for defeated or tired, and the Paraguayan herbal drink.

clue.text: One's into a Pres. abroad (or was)

definitions.text: One's into a Pres. abroad (or was)

indicators.note: abroad can mean widely scattered, so the letters are spread out anew

explanation.surface: Someone devoted to a foreign president, or who used to be.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes a supporter of Juan Perón, Argentina's president; 'or was' allows for past followers.
explanation.definitionFit: A Peronista is a supporter of the Argentine president Juan Perón and his political movement.

clue.text: Chime bringing together elements from district in kirk

indicators.note: parts of neighbouring words are joined, so a run of letters is taken across them

parts.note: letters spanning the end of district, all of in and the start of kirk

explanation.surface: Church bells ring out across a Scottish parish.
explanation.walkthrough: A kirk is a Scottish church, which suits the chime of the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Tink is an imitative word for a light ringing or clinking sound, the same as a small chime.

clue.text: Stone erected above US writer possibly, extremely rigorous

parts.note: ST abbreviates stone, a British weight of 14 pounds
first name of Hemingway, for example

explanation.surface: A tombstone set up over an American author's grave.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'above' puts one piece before the next. A stone is a British unit of weight, 14 pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Sternest is the superlative of stern, meaning most strict or severe, i.e. extremely rigorous.

clue.text: Directed round old bear bent over

indicators.note: one item goes round, enclosing the next

parts.note: ean is an archaic verb meaning to bear young

explanation.surface: Someone guided an elderly bear that was stooping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bear' looks like the animal, but it is the verb, to give birth.
explanation.definitionFit: To have leaned is to have inclined the body forward or sideways, i.e. stooped.

clue.text: Persecuted Christians adroitest when hiding round Rome's capital

indicators.note: to hide something is to keep it inside you
turning things round can scramble them, so these letters are rearranged
a capital is the head of something, so only the first letter is taken

explanation.surface: The cleverest of the early believers hide around the city of Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: Traditores were early Christians who, under Roman persecution, handed over scriptures or fellow believers to the authorities.

clue.text: S. American diplomacy? It's aimed to deter rebellious behaviour (7, two words)

definitions.text: It's aimed to deter rebellious behaviour

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro, a South American city

explanation.surface: South American diplomatic manners meant to quell unrest.
explanation.walkthrough: The Riot Act was a 1714 British law requiring unruly crowds to disperse once it was read out.
explanation.definitionFit: Reading the riot act was meant to deter rioting; idiomatically it is a stern warning to stop misbehaving.

clue.text: Star with jinx goes round unplaced after run here?

definitions.text: Star with jinx goes round unplaced after run here?

indicators.note: the word before encircles the item that follows

parts.note: R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for a run
an ace is a star performer
in form guides 0 marks a horse that finished out of the places

explanation.surface: A star horse, apparently jinxed, finishes nowhere after racing at this venue.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the place: a favourite seemingly cursed comes home unplaced at the track.
explanation.definitionFit: A racecourse is the track where horses run and where a fancied star may finish out of the places.

clue.text: King excessively topping Queen or Knave

parts.note: R for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Card names: a king lying too high on a queen or jack.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'topping' means placed above, so the first pieces come before the queen.
explanation.definitionFit: A knave is a dishonest scoundrel, and a rotter is a contemptible, untrustworthy person.

clue.text: I'm involved with a run requiring some guts

indicators.note: involved means intricate or tangled, so the letters are twisted together in a new order

explanation.surface: A runner says that going for a run takes courage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guts' suggests nerve, but it means stomachs.
explanation.definitionFit: Rumina is a plural of rumen, the first stomach of a cud-chewing animal, so these are particular guts.

clue.text: It protects driver in the outback, and sounds like rumpus without breadth? (6, two words)

definitions.text: It protects driver in the outback

indicators.note: without means lacking, so a letter is removed
says outright that the answer is said the same as the result

parts.note: rhubarb is noisy talk or a row; without breadth loses its final B

explanation.surface: An Australian driver's safety device, apparently pronounced like a word for uproar.
explanation.walkthrough: RHUBARB (a commotion) minus B is RHUBAR, said like ROO BAR. A roo bar is the metal grille fitted to Australian vehicles against kangaroo strikes.
explanation.definitionFit: A roo bar is a strong metal frame on the front of a vehicle guarding it and its occupants from collisions with kangaroos.

clue.text: Skene-dhu may be stuck in here — and what results when one's stuck in?

definitions.text: Skene-dhu may be stuck in here

indicators.note: something stuck in is pushed inside something else

parts.note: a wound is what results when a blade is pushed in

explanation.surface: Where a Highlander's knife sits, and the wound that would follow if it were used.
explanation.walkthrough: A skene-dhu is the small dagger tucked into the top of a Highland kilt stocking; 'cuit' is Scots for ankle or lower leg.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scots cuit means the ankle or lower leg, near where the stocking dagger is worn.

clue.text: Not a bad shot, something very impressive but missing wicket

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so a letter is left out

parts.note: a winner is a great success
W is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for a wicket

explanation.surface: A cricketer plays a fine stroke yet fails to take a wicket.
explanation.definitionFit: In target shooting an inner is a shot hitting the ring next to the bullseye, a good but not perfect hit.

clue.text: Part of hop, no good in a drinking session

indicators.note: no means none present, so that letter is taken out

parts.note: a binge is a bout of heavy drinking

explanation.surface: Hops, used for beer, have no place in a bad night out drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: A bine is the twining climbing stem of a plant, especially the hop.

clue.text: One duck nips another producing separated fibre

indicators.note: to nip is to pinch, holding something between the jaws

parts.note: a duck is a nil score in cricket
another duck, this time the zero shape O

explanation.surface: One duck pecks another, sending feathers flying.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a duck is a score of zero, so one is NIL and the other is the round letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: Noil is the short fibre combed out from long wool or silk, the separated short stuff.

clue.text: Con artist's regularly shedding such seedy stuff

indicators.note: dropping letters at regular intervals leaves every other one

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: A swindler casting off disreputable seedy goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seedy' suggests shabby, but here it means made of seeds.
explanation.definitionFit: Oats are the grain of a cereal grass, literally seeds, and are often scattered as seed.

clue.text: Bird that can't fly — it's limited in speed

indicators.note: something limited in is confined within bounds

explanation.surface: A grounded bird whose pace is restricted.
explanation.definitionFit: Ratites are the flightless birds such as ostrich, emu and kiwi, with a keel-less breastbone.

clue.text: One poetic tree like another

explanation.surface: One tree resembles a different tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Another' carries on from 'tree', so it means a second tree; ASPINE is Spenser's word for the aspen.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspine is an old poetic form found in Spenser for the aspen, a poplar with trembling leaves.

clue.text: Plunge into trough — baconers do? O, this boar possibly

indicators.note: this stands for the answer itself, which sits in the mix between O and boar
possibly suggests the letters could be arranged otherwise, so the phrase baconers do is a jumble

parts.note: taken as written: the letters of this pig phrase are the pool

explanation.surface: Pigs being fattened for bacon dive into the feeding trough, as a boar might.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: 'baconers do' is 'possibly' (an anagram of) O + 'this' (the answer) + boar, so take O and BOAR out of its letters and rearrange what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Scend (also send) is the sudden downward lurch of a vessel into the hollow between waves.

clue.text: Turkey has a certain stuffing, something that adds quality

indicators.note: to have something as stuffing is to hold it inside

parts.note: TR is the international vehicle code for Turkey
one means a certain, as in one Mr Smith

explanation.surface: A Christmas turkey gets some particular stuffing that improves it.
explanation.walkthrough: Turkey looks like the roast bird, but it is the country.
explanation.definitionFit: A toner adds tone, a quality of colour or firmness, whether in photography, cosmetics or printing.

clue.text: Trap teasers set deviously taking in tons? Quite different (12, two words)

indicators.note: to take something in is to enclose it
arranged in a crooked way, so the letters are placed in a new order

explanation.surface: A trap for teasing puzzlers, cunningly laid with heavy weights.
explanation.definitionFit: Streets apart is an idiom for being very far from each other in quality or nature.
